title: Optimize: compute recommendation ROI via Standard Cost Model (what-if + breakdown)
author: Hassan Mirza
release_notes: Internal: Optimize ROI estimates now use Cost Model API standard primitives (estimate/breakdown/what-if). ROI numbers may shift slightly vs legacy estimator; visible only behind optimize.cost_model_roi_v1 flag.
description:
Summary: This PR switches Optimize recommendation ROI estimation to use the Standard Cost Model outputs (Cost Model API v1) instead of the legacy Optimize-only estimator. It introduces a mapping layer from Optimize recommendation configs (batching, caching, quantization) into cost-model what-if inputs, normalizes breakdown semantics (prefill/decode, cache hits, batch efficiency, overhead allocation), and adds regression tests against golden fixtures.

Why: We currently compute ROI in Optimize with a separate estimator that diverges from Console telemetry/billing definitions (prefill vs decode, how cache hits are attributed, and how overhead is allocated). This caused inconsistent numbers across product surfaces and support escalations. The goal is to make ROI consistent with the canonical cost primitives so that: (1) Optimize and Console show the same breakdown taxonomy, (2) Finance can reconcile reporting windows, and (3) we can rely on versioned schemas and drift monitoring.

Scope: - Replace Optimize ROI engine cost primitives with calls to cost-model-client (new shared library). - Add RecommendationConfig -> WhatIfRequest mapper with explicit semantics and bounds. - Update ROI output object to store cost-model schema version + breakdown keys for traceability. - Add confidence handling: for what-if responses that include CI bounds, we surface the interval and apply conservative ROI (use upper-cost bound for current and lower-cost bound for proposed) when rendering "savings" in UI.

Non-goals: - No changes to billing/invoicing. - No customer-facing pricing calculator.

Implementation details: 1) New interface: CostModelRoiEstimator uses CostModelClient.WhatIf() with a workload summary instead of raw per-request replays. Workload summary is assembled from Optimize traces (tokens, seq-length histogram, concurrency hints) and bounded to avoid high-cardinality blowups. 2) Mapping layer: Optimize recommendation types map to cost-model knobs as follows: - Batching: max_batch_tokens, max_batch_size, and scheduler_policy set from recommendation payload; we clamp to cost-model policy guardrails and annotate if clamped. - Caching: prefix_cache_enabled, target_cache_hit_rate, and cache_key_strategy mapped; warm-rate is NOT modeled in v1 (see open questions). If recommendation includes warm-rate assumptions, we drop it and emit a debug note. - Quantization: quant_profile_id set using model-catalog stable profile IDs; we disallow changing model family in v1 ROI (only same base model + different quant profile). 3) Breakdown alignment: We consume cost breakdown from cost model and translate into Optimize UI sections (Compute, Memory, Network/IO, Overhead). Prefill/decode split is preserved and available behind a debug toggle. 4) Versioning: We pass requested_schema_version="cost-model/v1"; if the service responds with a newer minor version we accept unknown fields and log the negotiated version. 5) Failure/fallback: Behind feature flag optimize.cost_model_roi_v1 (default off). On cost-model call failure or timeout, we fall back to legacy estimator and emit metric optimize.roi.cost_model_fallback=1 with error_code label.

API usage: Endpoint used: POST /internal/cost-model/v1/what-if (client: pkg/costmodel/client). Timeout 250ms, 2 retries w/ jitter, circuit breaker uses existing internal policy. We cache per-(model_id, workload_fingerprint, recommendation_fingerprint) for 10 minutes in Optimize backend to reduce call volume on list pages.

Testing: - Added unit tests for mapping rules + clamping. - Added integration-ish tests with recorded fixtures from cost-model staging (golden JSON) to ensure breakdown keys remain stable. - Added a regression test that validates ROI is monotonic for a small set of known-good scenarios (e.g., enabling prefix cache with higher hit rate should not increase predicted cost).

Observability: - Metrics: optimize.roi.cost_model_latency_ms, optimize.roi.cost_model_errors_total{code}, optimize.roi.cost_model_schema_version{version}, optimize.roi.cost_model_fallback_total. - Structured logs include cost_model_request_id and negotiated schema version to correlate with cost-model service logs.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind flag. 2) Enable in staging for internal accounts; compare ROI vs legacy estimator; validate drift against observed spend windows. 3) Canary 5% of Optimize sessions for hosted-only; then expand to dedicated/private after verifying tenancy metadata is correctly passed.

References: - ENG-4826 (Optimize adoption) - ENG-4824 (what-if endpoint) - PR #28462 (cost-model client library) - Slack: eng-ml thread 1768474332 (quant uncertainty) - Support: SUP-31877 (ROI too optimistic; cache warm assumptions)

Checklist: - [x] Feature flag added and default off - [x] Metrics and logs added - [x] Unit tests + fixtures - [x] Docs note added to internal Optimize runbook (follow-up) - [x] Backward compatibility: legacy estimator retained

Open questions / follow-ups: - Warm-rate modeling for cache recommendations (requested by Optimize) intentionally excluded from v1 to keep cost-model complexity bounded. We should revisit after v1 launch; likely needs a separate workload-state model rather than a single scalar. - Quantization quality guardrails: cost-model returns confidence interval but not quality risk; we will add "quality_gate_status" to ROI explanation once cost-model exposes it.
commits: optimize/roi: add CostModelRoiEstimator and feature flag wiring
optimize/roi: map recommendation configs to cost-model what-if request (with clamps + annotations)
optimize/ui: consume breakdown taxonomy from cost-model and render conservative ROI bounds
tests: add golden fixtures + mapping regression suite
review_conversation:
Ethan Park (review): The mapper needs to be explicit about which fields are derived vs user-provided; otherwise we risk silently changing semantics. Also please ensure we pass tenancy metadata (account_id, deployment_mode) through to cost-model; without it overhead allocation will be wrong. Author (reply): Added a MapperAnnotation object in logs + debug response, and ensured CostModelClient call includes tenant_context with deployment_mode and billing_tier. Added unit test asserting the context fields are present.

Aditya Rao (review): For UI, we should avoid showing inflated savings when confidence is wide; can we make conservative ROI the default? Also, what happens if cost-model times out on list pages? Author (reply): Implemented conservative ROI calculation when CI bounds present; if absent we keep point estimate. Added 10m cache keyed on workload+recommendation fingerprint; list pages hit cache mostly. Timeouts fallback to legacy estimator with metric + warning banner in debug view.

Dr. Maya Srinivasan (review): Quantization mapping: ensure profile IDs are stable and validated against model catalog; do not allow switching base model. Also please document how uncertainty is handled. Author (reply): Added validation: quant_profile_id must be in catalog for the model_id; otherwise reject with RecommendationInvalidConfig. Added docs in code comment + log field roi_uncertainty_policy="conservative".

Jonas Weber (review): The cache warm-rate field is present in recommendation configs. If we ignore it, we should make that visible somewhere so CS can explain discrepancies. Author (reply): Added annotation "dropped_fields=[cache_warm_rate]" and surfaced in internal debug JSON response; also added a note to the recommendation explanation string.

Logan Wright (review): Please ensure breakdown keys match ADR-022 taxonomy; I see 'gpu_seconds' vs 'gpu_time_seconds' in one fixture. Author (reply): Updated fixtures to current service output keys and added a test that fails if unknown top-level breakdown categories are returned.

Final: Ethan approved after changes; Aditya approved with a follow-up to add an internal doc page; Maya approved.
